subject: Starlite staging gate: SSO/SCIM & IP cutover sequencing
messages:
From: Laurence Park <laurence.park@starlitehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: starlite-it-team@starlitehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Starlite staging gate: SSO/SCIM & IP cutover sequencing

Hi Irene + Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. We want to lock down the sequencing for our staging gate next week so the SSO, SCIM group provisioning, IP allowlist, and the new service-account pattern are all exercised before prod cutover. Key constraints from our side:

- Staging environment mirrors prod networking, but we need to avoid any mass user reprovisioning in prod.
- Our security team requires an audit trail for SCIM provisioning and service-account actions.
- IP allowlist changes require a 48-hour notice for our perimeter team.

I've attached a short inventory (starlite_sso_inventory.xlsx) that lists the initial SAML SPs and the groups we plan to map over SCIM. Can you outline a step-by-step run for the dry-run and who owns each step? Specifically we need:

1) Exact SAML metadata we should import on your side.
2) Which IP/CIDR ranges Redwood will need to whitelist for staging.
3) Service-account creation pattern and required scopes.
4) A rollback plan if provisioning causes unexpected role assignments.

We are targeting a dry-run in staging on 2026-09-22 (UTC preferred) and a production cutover window on 2026-09-29. Open to adjustments.

Appreciate a concise mutual action plan we can include in our QBR on Friday.

Best,
Laurence Park
Head of IT, Starlite Health

Attachments: starlite_sso_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet: SP list + group map)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Laurence Park <laurence.park@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Starlite staging gate: SSO/SCIM & IP cutover sequencing

Hi Laurence — thanks for the inventory and context. Quick response with a proposed mutual action plan and owners below. We'll keep this high level for your QBR and follow up with a technical runbook (Ben will draft).

Mutual action plan (staging dry-run target: 2026-09-22)
- 2026-09-18: Redwood requests SAML metadata + IdP signing cert (owner: Starlite IT).
- 2026-09-19: Redwood imports metadata into staging, validates ACS/Entity IDs, and shares test endpoints (owner: Irene Choi).
- 2026-09-20: SCIM scope review — Redwood to confirm which attributes will be provisioned and group sync rules (owner: Monica Patel).
- 2026-09-21: Service-account creation in staging (ephemeral SA recommended), assign least-privilege roles, and run smoke provisioning (owner: Ben Carter).
- 2026-09-22: Dry-run: execute SCIM push for a 10-user test group, validate role mappings, collect audit logs. Redwood to provide step-by-step checklist and rollback commands.

IP allowlist request (staging)
- Please whitelist these outbound IPs for staging: 34.82.112.0/24, 34.82.113.0/24. If your perimeter requires single IPs, we can provide NATed addresses.

Service-account pattern
- We recommend an ephemeral service account per job (prefix: redwood-onboard-<customer>-stg), rotated weekly for staging, monthly for prod, and bound to scoped roles only (SCIM:Provisioner, Logs:Read).

Rollback plan (summary)
- Disable SCIM push (Redwood console toggle) -> Revert group membership via SCIM delta reversal command -> Restore from provisioning snapshot if needed. Ben will document exact CLI/API calls in the runbook.

Deliverables we will send by 2026-09-18
- Technical runbook (runbook-staging-cutover.md)
- Audit log snapshot template and retention options
- Test checklist and rollback steps

If that timeline works for you, we'll lock calendar invites and advance to the smoke test configuration.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Laurence Park <laurence.park@starlitehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Starlite staging gate: SSO/SCIM & IP cutover sequencing

Irene / Monica — adding a few technical notes I want in the runbook. I will turn these into a short markdown checklist (runbook-staging-cutover.md).

- Service accounts: create redwood-onboard-starlite-stg-01 (ephemeral, TTL 7d), bind only SCIM:Provisioner and Audit:Write. Store credentials in your vault; Redwood will fetch via KMS integration for the dry-run.
- SCIM: limit to membership + email + displayName initially. Avoid pushing role attributes in the dry-run; map roles later after validation.
- IPs: If you need HTTPS egress to a single address, request NAT IP 34.82.112.7 and 34.82.113.9 (we can reserve these). Otherwise accept the /24 ranges listed.
- Audit: enable SCIM delta logs + token rotation events. We'll populate an example Splunk query in the runbook.

Also: include a quick verification step after the dry-run:
1) Confirm 10 test users were created/updated in SCIM and group membership matches expected.
2) Confirm access to a sandbox model endpoint using service-account token.
3) Pull audit logs for the provisioning window (time range + correlation id).

I'll attach the runbook shortly.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Onboarding Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good. A few quick confirmations from Starlite: 

- SAML metadata: https://drive.starlitehealth.com/saml/starlite-metadata.xml (IdP signing cert included).
- IP allowlist: we'll provision the two /24s you listed in staging by EOD 2026-09-18. If you can reserve the NAT IPs (34.82.112.7, 34.82.113.9) that would speed firewall rules for our team.
- Service-account access: we will create a vault entry and grant Redwood read access for the staging run only.
- Dry-run: 2026-09-22 02:00 UTC (we confirmed with our on-call). Please send the final runbook and a calendar invite for the smoke test.

Laurence Park
